The Appalachian Mountains are among the oldest surviving mountain ranges on Earth, with roots over 1.1 billion years old and major uplift beginning about 480 million years ago, making them far older than the Rockies or Himalayas.
How Old Are the Appalachians?
Geologic evidence shows that the Appalachians began forming 1.1 billion years ago during the Grenville orogeny
Their modern mountain-building phases began around 480 million years ago in the Ordovician Period 
Key orogenies that built the range include 
Grenville Orogeny (~1.1 billion years ago)
Taconic Orogeny (~480–440 million years ago)
Acadian Orogeny (~410–370 million years ago)
Alleghanian Orogeny (~325–265 million years ago)
These collisions raised mountains once comparable to the Alps or Rockies
